Let’s talk about Chapter 10: Sustaining Momentum—Making OKRs a Lasting Habit.
Now, you’ve made it through the OKR journey, but the real magic happens when those OKRs become more than just a one-time project. The goal? To turn them into a lasting habit—something that’s woven into the fabric of your organization.
So, how do you actually keep that momentum going?
First, try embedding OKRs into your organization’s natural rhythm. That means making them part of your regular planning, review, and team conversations. When OKRs are always on the agenda, they’re front and center—not just another document collecting dust somewhere.
Next, make it a point to celebrate progress and learning. Don’t just focus on whether you hit the numbers—recognize the effort, the creative ideas, and everything your team learns along the way. It’s amazing how a little acknowledgment can boost morale and encourage a growth mindset.
Remember, as your organization grows and changes, your approach to OKRs should evolve too. Keep asking for feedback, experiment with new ways of working, and don’t be afraid to adapt. Flexibility keeps things fresh and effective.
Another key is to develop internal champions—those folks who are genuinely passionate about OKRs. Support them, let them coach others, and encourage them to share what works. Their enthusiasm can be contagious, helping to keep the OKR spirit alive.
And don’t forget to connect your OKRs to a bigger purpose. Remind your teams how their goals tie back to your organization’s mission and values. Knowing that their work matters—that it’s part of something meaningful—helps everyone stay committed, even when things get tough.
Think of it like tending a garden. Your OKRs need regular care—some watering, a bit of pruning, and attention to whatever the season brings. Over time, with patience and steady effort, they’ll become part of your organization’s DNA, supporting growth and resilience year after year.
